title: Seats, Introductions & Operating Data
markdown:
Colette Exec runs two kinds of seats. **Owner seats** (CFO, COO) exist because no human holds the role: each owns a department's operating outcomes through goals, a weekly cadence and live data. **Partner seats** (CMO-partner, CPO-partner, CEO-advisor) support a human who owns the function; they draft, challenge and follow through, and the human decides. Seat prompts live in `prompts/partner_prompts.py` (owner seats extend the upstream CFO/COO prompts with an operating-mandate overlay), agents in `agents/partner_seats.py`. All seats share one rule set: no invented numbers, every recommendation ends in a named owner and date, and the decision priority stack (safety and legal, then privacy and trust, then "life feels handled", then growth) breaks ties.

### Operating data feeds
`openexecutive.feeds` pulls small read-only snapshots for the weekly check-ins: GCP spend from the Cloud Billing BigQuery export (`BILLING_EXPORT_TABLE`, Application Default Credentials), Stripe balance, subscriptions and open invoices (`STRIPE_READONLY_KEY`, a restricted read-only key), and Linear cycle health plus issues idle for a week (`LINEAR_API_KEY`). `FEEDS_BY_DEPARTMENT` maps feeds to departments; `department_check_in` renders them as an `<operating_data>` block in the user turn (never a cached system block). A feed that is unset, errors or times out becomes a labelled gap, never an exception and never a guessed number, and error text carries the status code or exception type only, so credentials cannot leak into prompts or logs. The Strategy check-in additionally receives a `<company_rollup>` of every other department's owner, goals and recent decisions.

### Introductions and working agreements
A partner seat is not useful until it knows how its human wants to work with it. `partners.intro` supplies the substance of a discovery interview, which the Executive runs conversationally when the speaker owns a seat with no agreement (a hint in the `<current_speaker>` block offers it once; "not now" is saved as a deferral and never repeated unprompted). `begin_partner_introduction` returns an honest inventory of what the seat has consumed and cannot see (charter, goals and whether they have values, which feeds are connected, gaps) plus the agenda: introduce the role as support, read back what the seat knows, learn what it still needs, learn how the person wants to work (cadence, style, initiative, boundaries, what stays private), agree on the first month, then read back and obtain an explicit yes. Only then does `save_working_agreement` persist it (`partner_agreements` table, versioned, with a review date). Both tools refuse anyone but the seat's own human (the principal may act for any seat). `router.route_to_specialist` prepends the active agreement as a `<working_agreement>` block to that seat's context, so what the person said changes the seat's behavior; it never overrides the priority stack, data discipline or the human's decision. Privacy is a behavioral instruction to the seat, not an access control: all seats share one company database.
